Subject: Buying Orbit: MAP draft, security gates, and next steps

Hi Anna — great to meet today. Quick recap and an initial draft of the mutual action plan attached. Key items below and proposed owners/timeboxes.

Top takeaways from today
- Primary outcome: Mediview is interested in a POC to validate live inference latency and data handling for PHI-adjacent telemetry.
- Decision drivers: predictable latency (p95 < 250ms), SOC 2 evidence, and predictable monthly unit economics for inference.
- Timeline: procurement and security gates are the two longest poles — suggested runway of 6–8 weeks to POC sign-off if gates move on schedule.

Proposed MAP (attached: MAP_draft.xlsx) — headline milestones
1) Kickoff workshop (week 0) — align success criteria & data scope — owner: Kimberly (Redwood) + Anna (Mediview)
2) Security intake & evidence delivery (week 0–2) — owner: Mediview security + Redwood SRE
3) Provisioning & dedicated test capacity (week 2–3) — owner: Redwood ops
4) POC run & quality validation (week 3–6) — owner: Mediview product + Redwood SE
5) Commercial review & term negotiation (week 6–8) — owner: Procurement/Finance (Mediview) & Sales (Redwood)

As next steps I suggest:
- You share the procurement & security contact emails so we can route the intake.
- If acceptable, we’ll schedule a 60-minute kickoff workshop next Tuesday (May 30) 10–11am PT.
- Marissa will prepare a short pricing appendix with reserved-capacity and burst options; Rishi will collect the SOC 2 evidence checklist and KMS/HSM options for private deployment.

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP_draft.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)]

Thanks,

Kimberly — attaching the pricing appendix as discussed. Quick notes:
- Option A (Reserved POC): $12,000/month for a dedicated 1xA100-equivalent pool; includes 2 TB of KV cache and priority scheduling during POC. Ideal if they need consistent p95 latency.
- Option B (Burst-on-demand): $0.0009/token with a daily cap; lower upfront but higher variance. Good for exploratory workloads.
- Suggested commercial cadence: POC discount (20%) if they commit to a 6–12 month reserved contract following POC.

I also added a short appendix on how reserved capacity affects latency and queueing behavior — happy to present that in the kickoff.
